gloss: to drive out; to throw out; to produce (a result)

definitions.gloss: to drive out, to throw out, to kick out
definitions.explanation: To forcefully expel someone from a place. Carries a rough, aggressive nuance.

definitions.gloss: to produce, to achieve (a record, score, or result)
definitions.explanation: To achieve a notable result through effort. Used in sports, business, and competitive contexts for impressive numbers or records.

examples.japanese: {家|いえ}から{叩|たた}き{出|だ}す。
examples.english: Throw someone out of the house.

examples.japanese: {不法|ふほう}{侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ}を{叩|たた}き{出|だ}した。
あんな{態度|たいど}では{店|みせ}から{叩|たた}き{出|だ}されても{文句|もんく}は{言|い}えない。
examples.english: With that kind of attitude, you can't complain about being thrown out of the shop.

examples.japanese: {好記録|こうきろく}を{叩|たた}き{出|だ}す。
{過去最高|かこさいこう}の{売上|うりあげ}を{叩|たた}き{出|だ}した。
{新人|しんじん}{選手|せんしゅ}がホームランを{叩|たた}き{出|だ}して{観客|かんきゃく}を{沸|わ}かせた。
examples.english: The rookie player hit a home run and got the crowd excited.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{家|いえ}から{叩|たた}き{出|だ}す (throw out of the house)
・{記録|きろく}を{叩|たた}き{出|だ}す (produce a record)
・{売上|うりあげ}を{叩|たた}き{出|だ}す (generate sales figures)
・ホームランを{叩|たた}き{出|だ}す (hit a home run)

USAGE NOTES:
Sense 1 is colloquial and rough — it suggests physical or forceful expulsion. Sense 2 is commonly used in sports journalism and business reporting, conveying the impression that the result was achieved through force or determination. The verb carries energy and impact in both senses.
